## Overview

[OpenFamily](https://github.com/NexaFlowFrance/OpenFamily) is a free, self-hosted family
organizer: calendar, shopping list, tasks, meals, budget. This integration brings into Gladys what
the household uses every day:

- **The family calendar** becomes a Gladys calendar, kept up to date, shown in the **Calendar**
  view and usable in scenes ("an event of the calendar is coming"). Recurring appointments and
  full-day events are supported, over one month of history and twelve months ahead.
- **Five dashboard widgets**: today's appointments, the shopping list, the tasks, the meals and
  the reward points.
  The shopping list and the tasks have a button to add an entry and a button to check one off.
  The tasks widget can be the one of a single family member. On a day without an appointment,
  the first one shows the next three.
- **Seven scene actions**: add an item to the shopping list, add a task, stick a note on the
  fridge, read the shopping list, read the tasks, read the menu, read the points. The last four
  hand their result to the next actions of the scene (to announce it on a speaker, for
  instance).
- **Three scene triggers**: an item added to the list, a task completed, a task due today.

Gladys never changes the OpenFamily calendar. It only writes to OpenFamily when you add or check
off an item or a task, from a widget or a scene, and when a scene sticks a note on the fridge.

This is the official OpenFamily integration, built and maintained by
[NexaFlow](https://nexaflow.fr), the team behind OpenFamily.

## Requirements

- Gladys Assistant 5.2.0 or later.
- An OpenFamily server in version **2.0 or later**, that Gladys can reach on your network. **API
  tokens** (Settings, then API tokens) came with version 2.0.
- An API token created by a parent account. Choose **Read and write** to add and check off from
  Gladys; a **read-only** token is enough to display.
- For the right times: OpenFamily stores the family's local times, and the integration reads the
  family's time zone from OpenFamily itself.

## Configuration

1. In OpenFamily, open **Settings → API tokens**, give it a name ("Gladys"), choose the scope and
   create the token. Copy it right away: it is shown only once.
2. In Gladys, open the integration page and fill in:
   - **OpenFamily address**: the address of the server on your network, for example
     `http://192.168.1.20:3000`, with nothing after the port. Gladys is the one that has to reach
     it, not your browser: `localhost` means the integration's own container, and a Tailscale
     address or a `.local` name is often known to your own devices only.
   - **API token**: the token you copied, starting with `ofk_`.
3. Click **Test the connection**: the message names the account the token stands for.
4. For the calendar, enable the integration in the **My calendars** block. The "OpenFamily"
   calendar appears, private at first: share it with the household to see it on the dashboard and
   use it in scenes. The calendar is the same for the whole family: **one user only** should enable
   it, or every event shows twice.
5. Add the widgets from the dashboard editor: they are named "OpenFamily: today", "OpenFamily:
   shopping list", "OpenFamily: tasks", "OpenFamily: meals" and "OpenFamily: points".

**A tasks widget per member.** In the settings of the "OpenFamily: tasks" widget, type a first
name as it is written on the Family page of OpenFamily: the widget then shows only the tasks
assigned to that person, and a task added from this widget is assigned to them. Add the widget
once per child to give each of them their own list. Without a first name, the widget shows the
tasks of the whole family, with the name of the person each one is assigned to.

**Adding a task.** The **Add** button of the widget offers the due date in a list: no due date,
today, tomorrow, Saturday or in a week. For another day, type the date as YYYY-MM-DD in the
field below: it wins over the list.

**Meals.** The "OpenFamily: meals" widget shows the meals planned today and tomorrow in the meal
planner of OpenFamily. The "Read the menu" scene action hands the menu of today or tomorrow to
the next actions: the whole menu, or breakfast, lunch, dinner and snack separately. A scene can
then announce dinner on a speaker at the end of the afternoon.

**Family members in scenes.** The "Task completed" and "Task due today" triggers give the
"Assigned to" variable, the first names of the members concerned. The "Read the tasks" and "Add a
task" actions take a first name, to read only one member's tasks or to assign one to them.

**Points.** The "OpenFamily: points" widget shows the reward points of the members who earned
some, the best placed first. With a first name in its settings, it becomes the card of one
member: their points, their days in a row with a task done, and the tasks a parent has yet to
approve. The "Read the points" scene action hands these points to the next actions, and the
"Task completed" and "Task due today" triggers give the "Points" variable: what the task is
worth.

**A note on the fridge.** The "Stick a note on the fridge" scene action adds a note to the family
notes of OpenFamily, "The washing machine is done" for instance. Everyone reads it in the app;
OpenFamily sends no notification for a note. You choose its color and how long it stays: until
tonight, for a day, for a week, or until someone removes it. The note is signed with the name of
the account that created the API token.

Optional settings:

- **Refresh interval**: how often OpenFamily is read, five minutes by default. Changes usually
  arrive within seconds, through OpenFamily's real-time channel.
- **Category of added items**: the OpenFamily category given to the items added from Gladys
  ("Autre" by default).
- **Hour of the "Task due today" trigger**: the hour from which a task due today fires the
  trigger, 7 by default, in the family's time. A scene that announces the day's tasks does not
  speak at midnight. The trigger fires once per task on that day, even when Gladys or the
  integration restarts in between.
- **Time zone of the family**: usually left empty, since the integration reads the family's time
  zone from OpenFamily. Fill it in only to read the times in another zone.

Reminders go through Gladys' native trigger **"An event of the calendar is coming"**, with the
shared OpenFamily calendar: you choose the delay and filter on the name.

## Troubleshooting

The message shown on the integration page says what is wrong:

- **"Seen from Gladys, localhost is the integration itself"**: replace `localhost` with the IP
  address of the machine running OpenFamily on your network.
- **"Gladys cannot find the OpenFamily server under this name"**: Gladys does not know this name,
  as often with a Tailscale name or a `.local` name. Use the IP address of the server on your
  network.
- **"The OpenFamily server does not answer"**: the machine running Gladys cannot reach this
  address. That is the case of a Tailscale address (`100.x.x.x`) when Gladys is not part of that
  Tailscale network, or of a firewall between the two machines.
- **"The OpenFamily server refuses the connection"**: the port in the address is not the right
  one, or OpenFamily is stopped.
- **"This address starts with https:// but the server answers in plain HTTP"**: write the address
  with `http://`.
- **"Gladys does not trust the HTTPS certificate"**: the certificate is self-signed or comes from
  a private authority. Use the `http://` address of the server on your network.
- **"The OpenFamily server cannot be reached"**: another network failure. Check the address, with
  nothing after the port, and that it answers from the machine running Gladys.
- **"This OpenFamily server is too old for API tokens"**: update OpenFamily to version 2.0 or
  later.
- **"OpenFamily refused the API token"**: the token was revoked, or the account that created it
  left the family. Create a new one and paste it in the configuration.
- **"This API token is read-only"**: displaying works, but adding and checking off need a **Read
  and write** token. After this message, the **Add**, **Check off** and **Done** buttons leave
  the widgets; they come back as soon as a **Read and write** token is saved in the
  configuration.
- **"OpenFamily answered with an error"**: the address is probably not the one of an OpenFamily
  server.

Other cases:

- **"Nobody in the OpenFamily family is named ..."**: the first name typed in the widget settings
  or in the scene action is not the one of any member. Write it as on the Family page of
  OpenFamily; capitals and accents do not matter. If two members share a first name, write the
  full name of the one you mean.
- **The meals widget is empty**: it reads the meal planner of OpenFamily, for today and tomorrow.
  A meal with neither a recipe nor a text is not shown.
- **The points widget says that the server does not give the points**: this version of
  OpenFamily has no reward points. Update OpenFamily.
- **Someone is missing from the points widget**: it only shows who has already earned or spent
  a point. To see a member at zero, type their first name in the settings of the widget.
- **Events show twice**: two users enabled the calendar. Disable it for one of them and share the
  remaining one with the household.
- **Times are shifted**: check the family's time zone in OpenFamily, under **Settings**, then
  **Time zone**. If **Time zone of the family** is filled in the integration's configuration, it
  is the one used: empty it.
- **A scene bound to "Task due today" does not start in the morning**: the trigger waits for the
  hour set in the integration's configuration, 7 by default.
- **A button answers that it needs a more recent Gladys**: widget forms exist since Gladys 5.2.
- **The calendar does not update**: use **Sync now** on the integration page, and check that the
  calendar is not switched off in "My calendars".

A problem, an idea: [https://github.com/NexaFlowFrance/gladys-openfamily/issues](https://github.com/NexaFlowFrance/gladys-openfamily/issues).

## Configuration settings

These are the settings OpenFamily asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Connect your OpenFamily server | `section` | No | OpenFamily is a free, self-hosted family organizer. In OpenFamily (2.0 or later), open Settings, then API tokens, and create a "Read and write" token for Gladys. Paste it below with the address of your server, as Gladys reaches it on your network. |
| OpenFamily address | `string` | Yes | The address of the OpenFamily server on your network, as Gladys reaches it, without anything after the port. Not localhost, nor an address only your own devices know (Tailscale). |
| API token | `secret` | Yes | Starts with ofk_. A read-only token shows the data; adding from Gladys needs "Read and write". |
| Refresh interval (min) | `number` | No | How often OpenFamily is read. Changes usually arrive sooner, through its real-time channel. |
| Category of added items | `string` | No | The OpenFamily category given to the items added from Gladys. |
| Hour of the "Task due today" trigger | `number` | No | The hour (0 to 23, in the family's time) from which a task due today fires the scene trigger, so that a scene does not speak at midnight. 0: as soon as the day starts. |
| Time zone of the family | `string` | No | Usually left empty: the integration reads the family's time zone from OpenFamily. Fill it in only to read the times in another zone. |

## How to install OpenFamily in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: OpenFamily appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/nexaflowfrance/gladys-openfamily:0.4.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/NexaFlowFrance/gladys-openfamily](https://github.com/NexaFlowFrance/gladys-openfamily).

OpenFamily requires Gladys `>=5.2.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

OpenFamily is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [NexaFlowFrance](https://github.com/NexaFlowFrance), not by the Gladys core team.
